UK GDP grew 0.4% M/M in July, accelerating from 0.3% in June and beating expectations for no growth, with expansion across services, production, and construction.

Services output rose 0.4%, led by a 3.7% jump in administrative and support activities and a 2.4% increase in information and communication, partly offset by a 1% decline in wholesale and retail trade.
Production increased 0.2%, supported by a 0.9% rise in manufacturing, while construction grew 0.1% as a 0.8% increase in repair and maintenance offset a 0.4% decline in new work.
On an annual basis, UK GDP expanded 1.6% in July, marking the strongest year-on-year growth since February 2025.

title: UK economy beats forecasts with 0.4% growth in July
